question: According to data from the Spanish Government itself, it has made payments amounting to 25 % of the total Recovery and Resilience Facility funds allocated to Spain. In other words, the Spanish government should invest more than EUR 121 000 million from this Facility in a year when it has so far only been able to make payments of EUR 42 000 million over four years. And all of this, bearing in mind that we are not even talking about final implementation data. In view of this: 1.
Does the Commission have forecasts regarding the final implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Facility in Spain?

Does it envisage that the Spanish Government will be able to implement 100 % of the EUR 163 800 million allocated to Spain by the agreed deadline, or, conversely, what is its forecast regarding funds that will remain unused?

Has the Commission received requests from the Spanish Government to extend deadlines, renegotiate the timetable of milestones and targets or inform it that it will renounce funds available in the form of loans?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.9.2025) Following the latest disbursement of EUR 23.1 billion to Spain on 8 August 2025, representing the fifth payment under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF)1, the total funds paid out to Spain under the RRF now stand at EUR 71 billion, which is 44% of the total allocation.

In view of the 2026 implementation deadline, the Commission published a Communication (‘NextGenerationEU - The road to 2026’, 4 June 2025) providing guidance to Member States to review their recovery and resilience plans and prepare their final payment requests in 2026.

Member States are invited to review their plans to include only measures achievable by 31 August 2026 and explore alternative measures to use their remaining financial allocations. The Commission is in constant contact with the Spanish authorities to prepare for the end of the RRF in 2026.
